correctness.rationale: The signature has only equality and two named equivalence predicates E,F; for k=1, all unary atoms are reflexively true. For k=2, comparing existence of equality/E-only/F-only/neither among fixed-pebble extensions separates precisely the four phases, including asymmetric singleton classes when m=2 or n=2. For k=3, R(x)=exists y not exists z(E(x,z) and F(z,y)) defines the deficient E-row, with dual C(x) the deficient F-column. Locally reusing the other k-1 variables within R/C counts up to k ordinary rows/columns; permanent k-pebble partial coordinate correspondences show no greater distinctions, even at arbitrary depth. Thus the two full/punctured clipped-pair grids have (k-1)^2+k^2 theories for k>=3, with displayed smallest representatives and strict hierarchy. The two included scripts inspect the exact structures and refine finite types; this is only bounded corroboration.
residual_risks: The k-variable game proof, not finite checking, bears the unlimited-depth conclusion.
The k=2 classification assumes the two named relations are not permuted.
